title: The Hereditary Prince's cipher letters to Wilhelmina, Berlin 1795-97 (KHA A32-630, 'Anciens dechiffrements'); includes DECODE R2236

documents.shelfmark: Koninklijk Huisarchief, The Hague, A32 Wilhelmina, inv. A32-630, scans 1-194
documents.route: Willem Frederik, Hereditary Prince (Berlin, Brunswick) -> Wilhelmina (England)

plaintext.source: Contemporary interlinear decipherments on 65 pages; Wilhelmina's clear write-ups 'Chiffre de Guillaume du ...'.

transcription.notes: Many groups struck through after deciphering; alignments rough (agents' own warning).

documents.shelfmark: Koninklijk Huisarchief, The Hague, A32 Wilhelmina, inv. A32-630, scans 195-387

plaintext.source: Interlinear pencil decipherments and write-ups; a few letters undeciphered (scans 264, 266, 272, 328, 333, 365).

transcription.notes: Larger list (entries to about 720, '0' separators); from 29 Apr 1797 4-digit groups.

documents.shelfmark: KHA (DECODE R2236, catalogued under Prins Willem V inv. 337); same text as A32-630 scans 89, 264, 269-270, 272

plaintext.source: No decipherment found in A32-630; Wilhelmina's precis of 23 Mar 1797 (scans 274-275) read the companion letter only in part.

transcription.notes: Copie No. 1 numbers up to about 391; scan 89 numbers up to about 2800.

system.summary: Euler word-list code: numbered list of words and names in alphabetical runs; a group is a whole entry, chosen letter positions of an entry, or an entry cut by k letters at the front (k)N) or back (N^k). 1795-96 list of about 250 entries; 1797 list larger.
system.notes: From June 1796 many letters carry dummy number pages over lemon-juice text ('les chiffres qui suivent ne disent rien'); those are left out.

prior_solution.where: Contemporary decipherments in the file itself (1795-96); R2236 Copie No. 1 not printed in Colenbrander, Gedenkstukken II (searched in full text)

conditions.human_role: Lead chosen by the user from the KHA sweep; user asked to pair cipher pages with write-ups, rebuild the list and retry R2236.

solution.what: Fetched all 387 KHA scans of A32-630 and R2236's four DECODE images.
Two agents indexed every scan (kind, date, decipherment present): index_a.tsv, index_b.tsv.
R2236 'Copie No. 1' compared with A32-630 scan 269: same text, same line breaks; R2236 = scans 89, 264, 269-270, 272.
Two agents transcribed the 65 interlined 1795-96 pages as cipher runs with the decipherment above and a group alignment (pairs_a.txt, pairs_b.txt; about 1,360 runs, 12,500 groups).

Strict table build from the alignments gave thousands of conflicts (marks dropped or misread on struck-through groups); rebuilt instead by majority vote per letter position (vote.py): 245 entries, 145 clean, same list as R2237 (10 angleterre, 11 berlin, 15 france, 162 elgin, 169 haugwitz). key_euler.tsv.

R2236 Copie No. 1 (numbers to 391) and scan 89 (to 2800) fall outside the 1795-96 list; the 1797 letters use a larger list (entries to about 720, '0' separators), which is the one to rebuild before retrying R2236.
Two agents transcribed 21 deciphered 1797-type pages (scans 195-278) with marks; faint text between lines recorded as PT (pairs97_a.txt, pairs97_b.txt).

Decoded 1797 groups (N<=249) with the 1795-96 list against their own line's faint text vs another line's: 6% vs 4% (1796 control 82% vs 21%). 1797 numbers diffuse (545 distinct in 1,585). The old list does not apply; whether the 1797 numbers are a new homophonic list or dummies over lemon juice is open.
R2236 Copie No. 1 transcribed from the KHA original (r2236_copie1.txt, 317 tokens, 154 distinct, plain numbers 1-391 among clear Dutch).
Copie No. 1 decoded with the 1795-96 list, big number + following small numbers as letter positions: nonsense. A separate Dutch code.

Capacity test on pp. 243/249/261: 50 of 52 lines have more faint-text letters than the groups can yield (bare entries counted as 10 letters); clear words in the number lines absent from the faint text; faint text runs past the numbers. The faint text is a separate sympathetic-ink letter and the numbers a cover; no 1797 list can be rebuilt from these pages.
Downloaded the full text of Colenbrander, Gedenkstukken II (1,166 pages, Huygens retroboeken) and searched for the clear Dutch frame of R2236 Copie No. 1: not printed.

Copie No. 1 statistics: 317 tokens, 154 types, 94 singletons, small numbers 35% of tokens, ten repeated 3-6 number sequences; stretches between clear words carry several words, so a word/syllable code of about 400 entries, not alphabetical one-part. Judged too short for a ciphertext-only solution; not pursued.
R2236 Copie No. 1 decoded with d'Yvoy's 1797-99 Dutch tables (yvoy1797 table_L, table_E): no sense. KHA catalogue searched for keys: none for this code or the 1801 list online.

outcome.method_basis: Work in progress: the 1795-96 list is rebuilt from contemporary decipherments; the 1797 numbered pages are covers over sympathetic ink, so R2236 Copie No. 2 has no key material; Copie No. 1 is a separate Dutch code.
outcome.notes: R2236 identified as copies in A32-630 (20 Mar 1797).
